The Federal Government has directed airlines operating domestic flights to adopt V-PASS, a passenger biometric verification system linked to the National Identification Number, and aimed at eliminating identity fraud and improving security across Nigeria’s airports. The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, disclosed this on Monday in a post on his X handle, following the unveiling of the system at the domestic terminal of the Murtala Muhammed Airport, Lagos. Keyamo said the system, known as the Airport Passenger Verification System, was linked to the National Identification Number of Nigerians and would be used exclusively for domestic flights. He said, “The system is a smart system that is linked to the National Identification Number (NIN) of all Nigerians, and it will be mandatory for all passengers to check in with their NIN. It is designed only for domestic flights.” The minister said the technology would help prevent passengers from boarding flights with fake identities and tackle touting and ticket racketeering. Keyamo said, “I have directed the NCAA to give all airlines in the country up till December 31st to key into the system.” He explained that the biometric verification system was designed to improve passenger processing, strengthen airport security and make air travel faster and safer. According to him, the project was executed through a Public-Private Partnership arrangement. The unveiling was attended by the Managing Director of the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria, Olubunmi Kuku; the Director-General of the Infrastructure Concession Regulatory Commission, Jobson Oseodion Ewalefoh; and other senior FAAN officials. The development follows the Federal Government’s approval of the deployment of the V-PASS system across domestic airports, announced in April 2026. At the time, Keyamo said the initiative was intended to address inconsistencies in passenger data and prevent unauthorised boarding by ensuring that travellers were properly identified. He also said the system would extend identity verification measures already in place for international travel to domestic flight operations.
